item.title: Commemoration in Tralee to mark 81st anniversary of death of Charlie Kerins
item.description: Kerry Sinn Féin is holding a commemoration this evening, to mark the 81st anniversary of the death of IRA volunteer Charlie Kerins. Advertisement Known as “The Boy from Tralee,” Kerins was executed in Mountjoy Jail on the 1st of December 1944 under orders from the de Valera government. The commemoration starts at the Pikeman Monument on Denny Street at 7pm, followed by a procession to the Charlie Kerins Monument on Strand Street. item.title: Kerry sign goalkeeper Harry Halwax
item.description: Kerry FC have signed goalkeeper Harry Halwax from Longford. The 23-year-old Dublin native made 42 appearances for the midlanders, and also has previous First Division experience with Cabinteely, where he played 13 league games in 2021. He has represented the Republic of Ireland at Under 16, 17 & 18 levels. item.title: Nature restoration charity launches initiative in Iveragh Peninsula
item.description: A nature restoration charity has launched its initiative in Kerry. Hometree’s latest project aims to restore native woodlands in the Iveragh Peninsula. The Iveragh Woodlands European Innovation Partnership hopes to revitalise up to 300 hectares of land. item.title: Six Kerry individuals and groups honoured at Ocean Hero Awards
item.description: Six individuals and groups from Kerry were honoured at this year's Ocean Hero Awards. Each year the Ocean Hero Awards highlight the contribution and dedication of Clean Coasts volunteers in caring for and protecting their coastal environment and heritage. Presentation College Tralee and Tralee Tidy Towns, won in the Campaign Ambassador Category for their ongoing efforts in promoting the Think Before You Flush Campaign. item.title: €200k allocated to KCC for Local Enhancement Programme
item.description: Over €200,000 in funding has been allocated to Kerry County Council under the Local Enhancement Programme for 2026. This funding will provide capital supports that are essential for many small community groups and organisations in the county, particularly those who serve disadvantaged communities in rural and urban areas. item.title: Today marks the centenary of the birth of Con Houlihan
item.description: Today marks the centenary of the birth of one of Kerry’s greatest writers, Con Houlihan. Widely regarded as Ireland’s greatest sports writer, the Castle Island man was renowned for his wit, intelligence and craft. Irish Times sports journalist Ian O'Riordan remembers Con as a man proud of his Kerry roots. Advertisement He’s particularly remembered for his columns for the Irish Press including his memorable report of the 1978 All-Ireland Senior Football Final between Kerry and Dublin. Advertiseme

item.title: Ballymac Are Munster Junior Champions
item.description: Ballymacelligott are the AIB Munster Junior Football Club Champions for 2025. They overcame the Cork champions, Buttevent, on a final score of 3-12 to 0-08 at Mallow, having led by a point, 1-04 to 0-06 at half-time. Advertisement

item.title: Villa Blow Away Gunners With Stoppage Time Winner
item.description: Aston Villa scored a 94th minute winner to beat Arsenal in the Premier League. Emi Buendia (PRON: Bwen-dee-ah) handed the league leaders just a second loss of the season. That victory also moves Villa up to second, just three points behind the Gunners. Advertisement

item.title: Hanrahan To Start For Munster In Euro Opener
item.description: Kerry-native JJ Hanrahan will start at Out-Half for Munster this afternoon in their Investec Champions Cup opener at Bath. He'll replace the injured Jack Crowley against the English Premiership champions. Kick-off is at 8 o'clock. Advertisement Leinster set off on another Investec Champions Cup adventure this evening, welcoming Harlequins to the Aviva Stadium. Leo Cullen's side have reached three of the last four finals in Europe's premier competition.

item.title: Munster Glory For An Ghaelteacht
item.description: An Ghaelteacht are the AIB Munster Intermediate Club Football Champions. The west Kerry side enjoyed a six point victory over their Cork counterparts Aghabullogue in Rathkeale winning on a 2-12 to 1-08 scoreline. Advertisement
